name: NanoEngineering - BS
department: Aiiso Yufeng Li Family Department of Chemical and Nano Engineering
narrative: To graduate, students must maintain an overall GPA of at least 2.0, and the department requires at least a C- grade in each course required for the major.

Every course required for the major (except NANO 4 and NANO 199) must be taken for a letter grade, including all CENG and technical elective courses. This also includes all MATH, BILD, CHEM, and PHYS courses. All courses used to fulfill major requirements must have a grade of C- or higher.

Effective winter 2026, NanoEngineering is designated as a screened major. Screened Major Eligibility Requirements: Overall UC San Diego GPA of 2.0 or above; Letter grade of C- or above in all screening courses. Required screening courses: First-year admits: MATH 20A-C, MATH 18; CHEM 6A-C, PHYS 2A, NANO 4; Transfer students: MATH 20A-D, MATH 18; CHEM 6A-C; PHYS 2A-C; NANO 4 or NANO 11 or NANO 15.
Transfer students must take NANO 4 and NANO 11 in their first year.
Please note that there was a curriculum change and students admitted prior to fall 2020 should review previous catalog copies regarding requirements.

requirement.notes: sixty units: twenty-four units of mathematics (MATH 20A-E and MATH 18 (formerly MATH 20F)), sixteen units of physics (PHYS 2A-D), sixteen units of chemistry (CHEM 6A-C, 7L), and four units of biology (BILD 1)
twelve units: computer programming, circuit analysis and circuits lab
forty-seven units: a one-unit seminar (NANO 4) and nine core courses (NANO 11, 20L, 102, 104, 110, 111, 112, 115L, 117, 119, 120A, 120B, and 148)

items.text: NANO 199 can be used as a NanoEngineering elective only under restrictive conditions. Two NANO 199 courses are required to fulfill the NanoEngineering elective major requirement and must be done in consecutive quarters.

requirement.label: NanoEngineering electives
requirement.notes: twenty units: The five elective courses requirement must be chosen from among the upper-division NANO courses offered by the department (NANO courses numbered 100 through 199). Courses such as NANO 195, 197, and 198 are not approved to meet upper-division NanoEngineering elective major requirements.
